title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Claude adds two beta features: live dashboards that connect to BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, and Salesforce and auto-update with numbers linked to their queries (paid plans), and Claude Motion, which turns a prompt into editable code-built animated explainers exported as MP4 (Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design have left beta and are available on all plans including Free, with the standalone Design site remaining until Dec 14. This lets non-technical staff get data answers and presentations without SQL or tickets.

title: Automating eval design and hillclimbing with Claude
summary: The eval-design playbook is implemented as the /claude-api build-eval and /claude-api hillclimb commands in Claude Code's claude-api skill. build-eval interviews the user, samples inputs, picks the cheapest grader, and checks baseline consistency and headroom, while hillclimb splits train and test data and keeps a patch only if both improve, guarding against overfitting. In the example, moving from Opus 4.8 at 4.6 cents per ticket to Sonnet 5 at about 1 cent raised held-out score from 78.6% to 90.5%, and users start by running claude update.

title: How an Anthropic BDR in Japan runs his day with Claude Managed Agents
summary: An Anthropic business development representative in Japan built 'Nakama,' a six-agent fleet on Claude Managed Agents (beta) for lead routing, email drafts, CRM updates, and follow-ups, moving from laptop prototypes to managed deployments with cloud schedules, shared memory, versioned instructions, and credential vaults. Models are tiered by task (Sonnet for rule-based agents, Opus for judgment, and Sonnet with an Opus advisor for replies), and he reports saving about 60 hours per his weekly log while still reviewing drafts and judgment items. It shows non-developers can run scheduled business agents, with single-purpose agents and shared memory helping.

title: Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI
summary: Uber CISO Philip Martin discusses insider threat risk for AI agents, pairing Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with Uber's open-source AI Detection and Response (ADR) tool. Uber keeps data inaccessible to Anthropic without permission and decides responses to triggers, with classifier output feeding its ADR and LLM gateway. Martin argues models need insider-risk monitoring like employees, with real-time intervention.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released claude-haiku-5-5, billed as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, at about 75% lower cost than Haiku 4.5 on average and as the first Haiku-class model with adjustable effort. Sonnet 5.5's cache-read price was halved, Max and Team get monthly API credits, and OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) rose from 15.7% to 72.4%. It suits high-volume, latency-sensitive work and subagent roles, while Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex coding.

title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
summary: OpenTelemetry tracing for Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and SDKs is now in public beta. Teams add a destination in Claude Console, and each agent turn, model call, and tool use is exported as an OTel trace with latency, tokens, and IDs, following OTel GenAI semantic conventions for backends such as Grafana Cloud, Datadog, Langfuse, Splunk, or any OTLP endpoint. This lets teams review agent behavior before granting more access and track org-wide token usage.
